content.intro: In this lesson, you will study thresholds, Calibration, and Uncertainty within Model Evaluation, Validation, and Reliability. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Evaluation is part of system design, not an afterthought. A metric is useful only when it reflects the goal, data conditions, and error costs.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: A classifier threshold maps scores to actions, while calibration asks whether predicted probabilities align with observed frequencies. Uncertainty estimates are conditional on data and model assumptions, not correctness guarantees.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics covered in this lesson

items.title: Threshold selection
items.text: Threshold selection is one of the concepts used to reason about thresholds, calibration, and uncertainty. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Precision–recall trade-offs
items.text: Precision measures how many predicted positives are correct; recall measures how many actual positives are found. Raising one can lower the other as the decision threshold changes.

items.title: Confidence intervals
items.text: A confidence interval communicates sampling uncertainty under a specified statistical procedure and its assumptions. It is not a guarantee that an individual prediction is correct or that a particular interval has a fixed probability after observing it.
